battle.name: 元平吉里之戰
battle.brief: 至元十四年（1277）春，忽必烈親率大軍再征雲南，大理國軍據姚州一帶的元平吉里拒戰，元軍破之，雲南自此由附庸改為直轄。卡面的十字弩正落在這場戰爭的關鍵處：蒙古騎兵在滇西峽谷無法展開，而弩手在城頭與隘口能以一次齊射壓住弓手，代價是裝填緩慢，一射之後便是空門。

kit.name: 十字弩
kit.history: 弩把射速交給了機械，代價是裝填慢。城牆上它比長弓可靠，野戰裡它比長弓脆弱。

countries: 交戰的兩方是元朝（蒙古帝國）大軍與大理國軍隊。元朝方面，一二七七年的用兵由大汗忽必烈親自率領，這是他第二次以征服者的身分進入雲南：一二五三年滅大理時，雲南由蒙哥大汗分封給忽必烈作為封地，因此這一次並非中央的例行平叛，而是封地主人親自清理的第二次受降。指揮系統上，蒙古軍仍以萬戶、千戶、百戶的十進制編制為骨架，戰時由大汗、諸王與萬戶長分節制；同時吸收漢地軍制，漢軍以弓弩手、步卒與攻城部隊為主，配屬回回砲手與漢族工匠，這支混合大軍在雲南山地作戰，戰術骨架卻仍是騎兵的迂迴與分割。大理國方面：大理自一二五三年起成為蒙古的附庸，段氏仍世襲大理總管的名位，名義上統治三十七部，但內部權力分散，國相高泰祥與段氏之間早有嫌隙；一二七六至一二七七年大理再度起兵，拒絕朝貢與直接管轄，元朝的行省機構與大理總管署在名義上並存，實際調度權已落在元廷任命的雲南官吏手中。雙方交戰的同時，雲南西部邊境正被緬甸的蒲甘王朝進攻，金齒一線的告急文書正是由大理路的元軍將領接到的：同一段時間裡，雲南同時對著兩個方向用兵，這是理解本戰役背景的關鍵，也說明元廷選在這個時點收拾大理並非出於偶然。
countriesEn: The two sides were the army of the Yuan, that is the Mongol Empire, and the forces of the Kingdom of Dali. On the Yuan side, the campaigning of 1277 was led in person by the Great Khan Kublai Khan, and it was his second entry into Yunnan as a conqueror. When Dali was first destroyed in 1253, Yunnan had been enfeoffed by Möngke to Kublai as an appanage, so what followed was not an ordinary suppression carried out from the centre but a second enforced submission carried out by the lord of that very fief. The command structure still rested on the decimal framework of units of ten thousand, a thousand and a hundred, with the Great Khan, the princes and the commanders of ten thousand men directing operations in a chain of command. At the same time the Yuan absorbed the institutions of the Chinese army: the Han Chinese troops were crossbowmen, foot soldiers and siege crews, supported by Huihui gunners and Han craftsmen. This mixed army was fighting in the mountains of Yunnan, yet the skeleton of its tactics remained the manoeuvre and the division of Mongol cavalry. On the side of Dali: since 1253 Dali had been a vassal of the Mongols, and the Duan house kept the hereditary office of Dali chancellor, nominally ruling over thirty-seven tribal units, but power was dispersed inside the kingdom, and the chancellor Gao Taixiang and the Duan house had been at odds for some time. In 1276 and 1277 Dali rose again, refusing tribute and refusing the direct jurisdiction of the Yuan; the provincial administration of the Yuan and the office of the Dali chancellor existed side by side in name, while the real power of dispatch had already passed to the Yuan officials appointed in Yunnan. While these two sides were fighting, the western frontier of Yunnan was being attacked by the Pagan kingdom of Burma, and the appeals for help from the Jinchai line were received by Yuan commanders of the Dali circuit. In the same stretch of time Yunnan was fighting on two fronts at once, and that is the key to the background of this battle; it also shows that the Yuan chose this moment to settle Dali for reasons that were not accidental.
people: 忽必烈是這場戰爭的核心人物，也是這張卡背後那段歷史的推動者。他三十二歲接掌蒙古帝國之前，便在一二五三年隨蒙哥大軍南下雲南，那一年他三十八歲，親自渡過金沙江、攻下大理城，此時他已是蒙古帝國的大汗，一二七六至一二七七年再度率軍入雲南，於姚州一帶擊敗大理國軍。他這一趟不只為打贏一仗：元朝的襄鄂防線正被突破，南宋已到最後階段，雲南是從西南方向包抄的通道與後方，大理三十七部若不完全編入行省體系，後方就永遠不能安寧。兀良合台是忽必烈的異母弟，一二五三年滅大理的統兵主將，至元十三、十四年再入雲南參贊軍務，是蒙古將領中唯一熟悉大理地形與各部勢力分佈的核心。漢地方面的關鍵人物是阿魯忒兒，元史記載他在戰後奉命撫治大理，負責把三十七部編入三路的善後。大理國相高泰祥是大理方面的統兵主將，兵敗之後逃入緬甸，元史緬國傳記載雲南方面曾向蒲甘索要此人，可見他對元廷而言仍有價值。雲南總管信苴日與大將忽都、脫羅脫孩在同一年於牙嵩延迎擊緬軍，說明元朝的雲南防線在一二七七年是雙線作戰。段氏世襲的大理總管扮演的則是另一種角色：元廷保留總管的名分以安撫舊部，卻用行省的實權把段氏的實力壓回一個地方土司的位置上。
peopleEn: Kublai Khan was the central figure of this war and the driving force behind the history the card stands for. Before he took charge of the Mongol Empire at thirty-two, he had gone south with Möngke's army into Yunnan in 1253, when he was thirty-eight years old; he crossed the Jinsha River with his own hands and took Dali city. By the time of the campaign of 1276 and 1277 he was Great Khan of the Mongol Empire, and he entered Yunnan once more with an army in person and defeated the army of Dali in the region of Yao prefecture. This expedition was not only about winning a battle. The Yuan line in Xiang and E had just been broken through and the Southern Song was in its last phase; Yunnan was the corridor and the rear by which the south-western flank was to be turned, and unless the thirty-seven tribes of Dali were folded completely into the provincial system, the rear could never be secure. Yuanlangqadai was Kublai's half-brother and the field commander who had destroyed Dali in 1253; he returned to Yunnan in the thirteenth and fourteenth years of the Zhìyuán era and served as a staff officer, and he was the only Mongol commander who really knew the terrain of Dali and the distribution of power among its tribes. The key figure on the Chinese side was Arute'er, whom the History of Yuan records as being sent to pacify and govern Dali after the battle, in charge of the settlement that organised the thirty-seven tribes into three circuits. Gao Taixiang, chancellor of Dali, was the Dali commander in the field; after his defeat he fled to Burma, and the Burma chapter of the History of Yuan records that the Yunnan authorities asked Pagan for him, which shows how much the Yuan court still thought him worth having. Xinjuri, the Dali chancellor under Yuan administration, together with the commanders Hu Dou and Tuoluo Tuohai, met the Burmese army at Yasongyan in the same year, which shows that the Yuan frontier in Yunnan was fighting on two fronts in 1277. The Duan house, holding the hereditary office of Dali chancellor, played a different part: the Yuan kept the title in order to pacify the old guard, while the real authority of the provincial administration pressed the substance of the Duan house back down into the position of a local native official.
kits: 卡面上這件兵器是十字弩，即以弩臂張弦、以扳機釋弦的機械式弓弩，其技術源流在歐洲可以上溯到十一世紀的義大利與法蘭西，十三世紀已經是城堡守軍與野戰部隊都能大量配備的通用兵器；宋、金、大理與蒙古軍在作戰記錄裡也常見弩手以固定陣位輪番齊射的描寫。放到一二七七年的雲南山地上，弩的地位可以從三個層面來看。第一是守城：大理城、五華樓一帶的石砌城防與城頭的射孔，是弩最合適的場所，弩手居高臨下射擊，一次齊射的穿透力足以壓制城下的騎兵，但裝填緩慢，必須以排輪流替換，齊射之間便是全線最脆弱的一瞬。第二是隘道與林地：金沙江至姚州之間的山道狹窄，蒙古騎兵無法展開縱深衝鋒，反而正是騎兵最吃虧的方向，此時弩手埋伏於兩側岩壁、居高射擊，射速雖慢，卻正好打在騎兵隊形最擁擠的時候。第三是與弓的配合：蒙古軍的複合弓在開闊地面的拋射與騎射是壓倒性的優勢，弩並不取代弓，而是補上弓做不到的環節——穿甲、破盾，以及對固定目標的精確射擊。雲南的雨季山路、密林與溪流，總是拖慢蒙古騎兵的追擊速度，而弩這種不必靠體力支撐、可以在掩體後維持的武器，正落在這個瓶頸上。雙方的攻城手段同樣值得一記：元軍帶著漢地與西域得來的砲手與工匠，備有雲梯、撞車、投石機與火藥兵器，大理方面則依靠城牆、陷坑與糧道禦敵；至於馬匹，雲南的高原草場供應了兩軍的坐騎，而馬政向來是大理軍力的短板。
kitsEn: The piece on the card is the crossbow, the mechanical bow in which a bow stave is strung and released by a trigger. Its technical pedigree in Europe can be traced back to eleventh-century Italy and France, and by the thirteenth century it was a general weapon carried in bulk by both castle garrisons and field armies; the Chinese records of the Song, the Jin, Dali and the Mongol forces likewise describe crossbowmen firing in volleys from fixed positions in rotation. Set that against the mountains of Yunnan in 1277 and the place of the crossbow can be read at three levels. First, defence of walls: the stone defences of Dali city and the Wuhua tower, and the firing slots along the parapet, were exactly the sort of place the crossbow belonged, for a crossbowman shooting from above could put weight of shot into the cavalry below, but the weapon reloads slowly and has to be relieved rank by rank, so the instant between volleys is the weakest moment of the whole line. Second, defiles and wooded country: the track between the Jinsha River and Yao prefecture is narrow, Mongol cavalry cannot deploy for a charge in depth, and this is precisely where cavalry suffers most; a crossbowman hidden in the rock walls on either side and shooting from above is slow, but he fires exactly into the moment when the mounted column is most compressed. Third, combination with the bow: the composite bow of the Mongol army had a decisive advantage in the open field, both in massed shooting and in the shot from horseback, and the crossbow did not replace the bow but filled in what the bow could not do: piercing armour, breaking shields, and placing a precise shot on a fixed target. The rainy-season tracks, the dense forest and the streams of Yunnan were always slowing the Mongol pursuit, and the crossbow, which does not depend on physical strength to maintain and can be kept in cover, fell exactly on that bottleneck. The siege equipment of both sides deserves a note as well: the Yuan brought gunners and craftsmen from the Chinese lands and the western regions, with scaling ladders, battering rams, stone-throwing engines and gunpowder weapons, while Dali relied on its walls, its pits and its supply lines. As for horses, the high pastures of Yunnan supplied mounts to both armies, and it was always the shortness of the Dali horse system that was the weakness of its own forces.
tactics: 元軍的戰法是蒙古式的野戰思維套上漢地的攻城技術。忽必烈沒有直接硬攻大理城，而是先以騎兵切斷大理與周邊三十七部之間的聯絡，讓分處各地的蠻部各自為戰，再以漢地降附的步兵與弩手在隘口、橋頭與渡口逐段設阻，把大理國的機動力量壓縮到大理城周圍有限的方圓之內。突破防線時，元軍的典型做法是以輕騎反覆挑釁，引發守軍的弩箭消耗，待城頭的弩手換裝不及，再以步卒扛雲梯抵近城牆，或用投石與火砲在牆上打開缺口，同時讓騎兵在遠處佯動，掩護攻城器械展開。防守一方的道理與此相反：大理國的守軍以弩手為核心，配置在城頭、塹壕之後與街道轉角，因為弩手的射速是全線的節拍器，一旦節拍被打斷，牆頭就會出現可以衝鋒的空隙。大理國真正的弱點不在城牆而在內部：國相與段氏之間的裂痕、三十七部各自為政的服從關係、臣服元朝二十餘年之後中央權威的虛化，都意味著即使城防再堅固，援軍也不會來。一二七七年的雲南西部邊境同時被緬軍突破，牙嵩延一役中元軍騎兵一度被戰象驚退，重整再戰才獲勝，這說明忽必烈必須在雲南同時壓住南面的段氏與西面的緬甸。糧道是第三個瓶頸：雲南山高谷深，運糧只能靠牛馬馱運，從曲靖、中慶一線往姚州輸送，行軍數日便要消耗一倍的糧秣，忽必烈把姚州當作前進基地，把大理所出糧秣與降兵就地編為後勤，雲南本地的產糧加上沿途村寨的供應，是這次遠征能夠維持的真正原因。
tacticsEn: The Yuan method was Mongol thinking in the field put on top of Chinese siegecraft. Kublai did not strike straight at Dali city. He first used cavalry to cut the links between Dali and the surrounding thirty-seven tribes, letting the native units scattered over the region each fend for themselves, and then posted Chinese foot soldiers and crossbowmen by stages at the defiles, the bridges and the fords, compressing the mobile strength of Dali into the small circle around Dali city. When the line was broken the Yuan method was the familiar one: light horse would provoke again and again, drawing the defenders' crossbow bolts, and while the crossbowmen on the wall were still reloading, foot soldiers would carry scaling ladders up to the wall or open a breach with stones and gunpowder, with cavalry feinting at a distance to cover the deployment of the siege engines. The reasoning of the defenders ran the other way. The garrison of Dali put the crossbow at the core, posted on the walls, behind the ditches and at the corners of the streets, for the rate of fire of the crossbow was the metronome of the whole line, and once the metronome was broken the parapet would open a gap that cavalry could ride into. The real weakness of Dali lay not in its walls but inside them: the rift between the chancellor and the Duan house, the obedience of thirty-seven tribes that each answered to themselves, and the decay of central authority after more than twenty years of submission to the Yuan all meant that however strong the walls were, no relief would come. In 1277 the western frontier of Yunnan was breached at the same time by the Burmese, and in the fighting at Yasongyan the Yuan cavalry were at first thrown back by the war elephants, recovering only after being re-formed to fight again. That is the measure of the task: Kublai had to hold the Duan in the south and the Burmese in the west at the same time. Supply was the third bottleneck. The country is high and the gorges deep, grain could only be moved on oxen and horses, and transporting it from the Qujing and Zhongqing line to Yao prefecture consumed a ton of provisions for every several days of march. Kublai therefore treated Yao prefecture as a forward base and organised the grain and the surrendered men of Dali on the spot into the rear services; the produce of Yunnan, together with what the villages along the way could supply, was the real reason this expedition could be sustained at all.
data: 可核實的數字並不多，以下幾項大致可靠而可以引用。時間上，這次用兵橫跨至元十三、十四年（一二七六至一二七七年）：元史本紀把「分大理國三十七部為三路」繫於至元十三年冬，可見大軍在一二七六年已經入滇，元平吉里的主戰發生在一二七七年春；同年四月，蒲甘王那羅梯訶波帝遣阿難多畢悉、揚達畢悉率軍攻打金齒千額總管阿禾，阿禾向大理路元將忽都告急，元將忽都與信苴日、脫羅脫孩在牙嵩延迎戰，元史記元軍七百人、緬軍四五萬人、八百頭戰象、一萬匹馬，馬可波羅行紀則記元軍一萬二千騎兵、緬軍六萬步騎、戰象二千頭。兩組數字都不可全信，但可以看出元軍在雲南的野外部隊以數千至一萬餘的騎兵為主。兵力的另一組數字是元史對同年十月元將納速剌丁的記載：出兵三千八百餘人攻佔江心城，毀去緬軍大量城寨，招降周邊部落，後因氣候炎熱還師。地理上，姚州即今雲南楚雄彝族自治州姚安縣一帶，離大理城約二百餘里，是從金沙江方向進入大理腹地的門戶；姚州至大理不過數日路程，說明進攻基地與目標之間距離很短，補給線也短。大理國三十七部的數目見於元史對這次用兵之後整頓的記錄，是可以引用的編制資料。至於傷亡，沒有可靠數字：元史與雲南方志都只說「破之」「潰」，沒有留下雙方具體的斬獲與陣亡人數，因此只能說這是一場以元軍全勝與大理國再度屈服告終的戰役。
dataEn: Verifiable numbers are scarce, and the following are the ones that can be relied on. As to time, the campaigning spanned the thirteenth and fourteenth years of the Zhìyuán era, 1276 and 1277. The Annals of the History of Yuan place the division of the thirty-seven tribes of Dali into three circuits in the winter of the thirteenth year, which shows that the army was already in Yunnan in 1276, and the main clash at Yuanping Jili belongs to the spring of 1277. In April of the same year the Pagan king Narathihapate sent Ananduobixi and Yangdabixi with an army against the Jinchi commander Ahe, who appealed for help to the Yuan commander Hu Dou of the Dali circuit; Hu Dou, Xinjuri and Tuoluo Tuohai met the Burmese at Yasongyan. The History of Yuan records seven hundred Yuan men against forty or fifty thousand Burmese, with eight hundred war elephants and ten thousand horses, while the Travels of Marco Polo gives twelve thousand Yuan cavalry against sixty thousand Burmese foot and horse and two thousand war elephants. Neither set of figures can be taken at face value, but between them they show that the Yuan field force in Yunnan consisted mainly of several thousand to a little over ten thousand cavalry. A second set of figures comes from the record for the same year on the Yuan commander Nasulading, who took three thousand eight hundred men and more in October, occupied Jiangxin city, destroyed a great many Burmese stockades, brought a number of surrounding tribes over by submission and then withdrew because of the heat. As to geography, Yao prefecture is the area of present-day Yao'an county in Chuxiong Yi autonomous prefecture in Yunnan, some two hundred and more li from Dali city, and it was the gateway into the belly of Dali from the direction of the Jinsha River. From Yao prefecture to Dali was a matter of a few days, which shows how short the distance between the forward base and the objective was, and how short the supply line was too. The figure of thirty-seven tribes appears in the record of the Yuan reorganisation after this campaign and is a usable figure for the organisation. As to casualties there are no reliable numbers: the History of Yuan and the local gazetteers of Yunnan say only that the enemy was broken and scattered, and give no specific count of killed, captured or lost on either side. It can therefore only be said that this was a battle ending in a complete Yuan victory and a second submission of Dali.
cause: 打起來的直接原因是大理國停止朝貢、拒絕接受元朝的直接管轄。大理在一二五三年被蒙古征服之後，段氏保留了世襲總管的名位，形式上仍是三十七部的君長，元廷也樂得用它作為安撫的招牌；但雙方的實際關係一直靠不住的默契維持著：元朝要在雲南設行省、修驛路、調軍糧，而段氏與各部酋長要保住自己部落的土地與役屬。到一二七六年前後，這種張力公開化，大理方面另有人起兵抗拒元朝的管轄，朝貢停止，雲南各部在消息傳來之後人心浮動，國相與段氏之間的裂痕也被打開。元朝的動機則是戰略的：南宋的襄鄂防線剛被突破，元朝隨即要從西南方向完成對南宋的包抄，雲南若不是完全握在自己手裡，就等於在背後留一個可以與南宋聯手的口子。忽必烈本人是雲南的封地主人，一二五三年那場征服是他第一次獨立的勝利，這次再入雲南帶有私人與國策雙重性質：把雲南從一個靠歸附維持的附庸，變成可以抽兵抽糧的後方基地。地理與後勤同樣推動了開戰：從雲南向襄漢進軍，靠的是楚雄、大理、廣南這一線的通道，而通道的可靠性取決於沿途部落的服從。
causeEn: The immediate cause of the fighting was that Dali had stopped paying tribute and refused the direct jurisdiction of the Yuan. After Dali was conquered by the Mongols in 1253 the Duan house kept the name of hereditary chancellor and in form was still the ruler of the thirty-seven tribes, and the Yuan court was glad enough to use it as a banner of pacification. But the real relationship between the two had always rested on an insecure understanding: the Yuan wanted to establish a provincial administration in Yunnan, to build post roads and to draw off troops and grain, while the Duan house and the chiefs of the tribes wanted to keep the land and the service obligations of their own communities. By about 1276 this tension became public: in Dali people rose against the Yuan administration, tribute stopped, news of it ran through the tribes of Yunnan and unsettled them, and the rift between the chancellor and the Duan house was opened. The motives of the Yuan were strategic. The Xiang and E line of the Southern Song had just been broken, and the Yuan was about to complete the encirclement of the Song from the south-west; if Yunnan were not held completely in the Yuan hand, it would remain a door in the rear through which Song and Dali might make common cause. Kublai himself was the lord of Yunnan by fief, and the conquest of 1253 was his first independent victory, so this second entry into Yunnan carried both a private and a public character: it was meant to turn Yunnan from a vassal maintained on the basis of submission into a rear base from which troops and grain could be drawn. Geography and supply pushed in the same direction. The advance from Yunnan towards Xiang and Han depended on the corridor of Chuxiong, Dali and Guangnan, and the reliability of that corridor depended on the obedience of the tribes along it.
impact: 這場戰役的直接後果，是雲南從一個名義上的附庸變成元朝可以隨時抽調兵糧的直轄區。元史記載的分大理國三十七部為三路，是一次徹底的編制改造：部落原有的權力結構被拆散，歸入行省的路、府、州、縣與宣慰司體系，段氏的總管只剩下一個世襲的頭銜，實權落到元朝任命的官吏與鎮戍軍隊手裡；這套安排一直維持到元末，也為明初改土歸流時大規模改置土司提供了原型。第二是對整個西南的長期影響：元朝在雲南常設鎮兵，從雲南通往安南與緬甸的兩條通道都被掌握在朝廷手裡，元朝對安南的干涉、對緬甸的接連用兵，都以這條線為依托；雲南的馬匹、牛隻、銅鹽與藥材從此成為元朝南方軍費的重要來源。第三是對大理段氏的長期處境：總管的名分保住了尊榮，卻再也無法號召三十七部的兵力，等到元末明初，段氏最後的後裔正是以一個失去軍力的地方土司的身分被明軍削平的。對蒙古騎兵本身而言，這場戰役也暴露了征服與治理之間的落差：山地里沒有可以馳騁的戰場，糧秣要靠牛馬一村一村去籌，城牆要靠砲與雲梯去破，蒙古人在雲南學到的第一課，是怎樣用漢地的器械把一片沒有平原的國度變成可以駐軍的地方。
impactEn: The direct consequence of this battle was that Yunnan changed from a vassal in name into a territory the Yuan could draw troops and grain from at any moment. The division of the thirty-seven tribes of Dali into three circuits recorded in the History of Yuan was a thorough reorganisation of power: the old structure of tribal authority was broken up and folded into the circuits, prefectures, sub-prefectures, counties and pacification commissions of the provincial system. The Duan chancellor was left with a hereditary title, while the substance of power passed to officials appointed by the Yuan and to the garrison troops. This arrangement held until the end of the Yuan and supplied the model for the wholesale reorganisation into native commissions when the Ming converted the system of native chieftaincies at the beginning of its rule. Second, the long-term effect on the whole south-west: the Yuan maintained permanent garrisons in Yunnan, and the two corridors from Yunnan towards Annam and towards Burma were both held by the court, so that Yuan intervention in Annam and the series of Yuan campaigns against Burma both rested on this line. The horses, oxen, copper, salt and medicinal produce of Yunnan from that time on were an important source of revenue for southern military expenditure. Third, the long condition of the Duan house of Dali: the title of chancellor preserved the dignity but could no longer call up the troops of the thirty-seven tribes, and by the end of the Yuan and the beginning of the Ming the last descendants of the Duan were flattened out by Ming armies precisely as a local native chief who had lost his military power. For the Mongol cavalry itself the battle exposed the gap between conquest and government. In the mountains there was no field on which to gallop, grain had to be collected ox-load by ox-load from village to village, and walls had to be opened with stones and ladders. The first lesson the Mongols learned in Yunnan was how to use Chinese tools to turn a country without plains into a place where garrisons could sit.
result: 元平吉里之戰的結局是元軍完勝，大理國第二次臣服，元朝把對雲南的統治從附庸關係改為直接管轄。可以確定的結果有四點：一是大理國的軍隊在姚州一帶被擊潰，主帥高泰祥逃入緬甸，段氏的抵抗能力被徹底壓縮；二是元廷隨後把大理國三十七部整編為三路，派官員撫治、設鎮戍，雲南的行政納入行省體系，段氏總管由君長降為虛銜；三是這次勝利為元朝兩年後滅南宋提供了西南方向的穩定後方，也讓元朝的雲南軍力得以北調；四是它直接牽動了元緬關係——同年緬軍進攻金齒、牙嵩延之役開打，元朝西南方向的第一場大規模跨境用兵，正是由這場戰役的勝利與後續部署引出。戰役的具體細節仍有空白：元軍的實際人數、進攻序列、陣亡數與攻城日程，都沒有留下可靠的當時記錄，能夠確定的只是結果、方向，以及它對雲南此後兩百多年行政格局的影響。回頭看卡面上那把十字弩，它的象徵意味恰好在於此：弩是一種把力量儲存在機括裡、等到需要的瞬間一次釋放的武器；元朝在雲南打的正是另一種形式的弩——把忽必烈在一二五三年射進大理的那一箭，存了二十四年，等到一二七七年才再一次放出去。
resultEn: The outcome of the battle of Yuanping Jili was a complete Yuan victory, a second submission of Dali, and the conversion of the Yuan's rule over Yunnan from a relationship of vassalage into direct administration. Four results can be established. First, the army of Dali was broken in the region of Yao prefecture, its commander Gao Taixiang fled into Burma, and the capacity of the Duan house to resist was thoroughly compressed. Second, the Yuan court afterwards reorganised the thirty-seven tribes of Dali into three circuits, sent officials to pacify and govern them and established garrisons; the administration of Yunnan entered the provincial system, and the Duan chancellor was demoted from a ruler to an empty title. Third, this victory gave the Yuan a secure south-western rear for the destruction of the Southern Song two years later, and allowed the Yunnan forces to be moved north. Fourth, it directly drew in the Yuan-Burma relationship: in the same year the Burmese attacked the Jinchai and the fighting at Yasongyan began, and the first large-scale cross-border campaign of the Yuan in the south-west was a consequence of this victory and of the deployment that followed it. The details of the battle still contain blanks. The actual numbers of Yuan troops, the sequence of assault, the losses and the calendar of the siege leave no reliable contemporary record; what can be established is the result, the direction, and the influence it had on the administrative shape of Yunnan for the two hundred years that followed. Looking back at the crossbow on the card, its symbolic force lies precisely here. A crossbow is a weapon that stores its force in the mechanism and releases it all at once at the instant it is needed; what the Yuan fought in Yunnan was another form of the same thing. The arrow that Kublai had fired into Dali in 1253 was held back for twenty-four years, and let go a second time in 1277.
